text:
customer_acme: Hey team — our rerank job is returning wildly off scores after we switched some flows to the new embeddings endpoint. Scores are sometimes >1 or negative. Not getting an error from the API, just weird numbers in the `scores` array. Any chance this is a precision/shape thing?

ashley: Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste the exact request payload you used for embed + rerank? quick question: are you calling embeddings with model `embed-large-v2` and then rerank with `rerank-legacy` or the new `rerank-v1`?

customer_acme: We use `embed-large-v2` for embeddings and then `POST /v1/rerank` with body like this: ```json
{
  "query_embedding": [0.001, 0.002, ...],
  "candidate_embeddings": [[0.002, 0.003, ...], [0.004, 0.005, ...]],
  "candidate_ids": ["c1","c2"]
}
```
No explicit model in rerank call (we pass embeddings directly). The embeddings endpoint indicates dim 1536 in metadata.

mahmoud: ok that helps. Reranker expects the same vector layout/scale it was trained on. If `embed-large-v2` returns 1536 dims and the reranker was trained on 1024-d vectors, dot products and any normalization will be meaningless — could produce values outside expected range. Can you confirm the shape (length) of the arrays your client actually sent?

customer_acme: Confirmed — our logs show `len(query_embedding)=1536` and candidates also 1536. We thought passing raw vectors directly would be fine.

tina: This is exactly the kind of mismatch that yields weird scores. Two things to check: 1) are you normalizing embeddings (L2) before sending to rerank? 2) what reranker variant are you referencing in your app config? There are at least two rerank models in prod that expect different dims.

customer_acme: We're not normalizing on our side. Our previous setup used `embed-old` (1024 dims) and the app had an internal assumption of 1024. When we swapped in `embed-large-v2` the assumption never got updated.

ashley: Ok actionable steps: 1) Stop new jobs that send mixed-dim vectors (to avoid corrupting evaluation). 2) You can either: a) call our embeddings endpoint with model that matches reranker dims (we can suggest mapping), or b) add a short adapter step to down-project or re-embed via a compatible model. 3) If you need immediate roll-back, switch to the previous embedding model id.

dev-oncall: From runtime logs we see the rerank service does a fast dimension check but doesn't fail hard — it silently computes dot products with truncated/padded arrays (hence unexpected magnitudes). We'll push a fix to reject mismatched dims with a 400 and clear error message in the next patch. For immediate help, here's a quick repro to replicate locally: ```bash
# fetch a query embedding from embed-large-v2
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["hello world"]}' > q.json
# fetch a candidate embedding from embed-old
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-old","input":["candidate text"]}' > c.json
# unpack lengths in jq
cat q.json c.json | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
```

mahmoud: Also watch for scaling differences. Some newer embed models return float16-like values serialized to float32 ranges after quantization backends; if your client expects normalized vectors you need to run L2 normalization prior to dot product. We recommended pipeline: normalize embeddings on client, then pass to rerank, or let rerank do normalization if you pass `raw=false`. We'll document this.

customer_acme: Good to know. One more problem: we saw a spike in cost/billing because we retried a lot when results looked wrong — any guidance for credits or an expedited rollback?

ashley: I'm escalating billing to finance. @ops-bot could you open a billing ticket referencing this thread and flag for credits review? :pray:

ops-bot: Billing ticket #BILL-998 opened, linked to support thread 1769501234. Tagging finance for credits review.

tina: For a short-term patch you can run a dimension guard on our side using a Lambda or our transform route: detect embedding length mismatch and either: 1) reject with clear error, 2) run an adapter (PCA projection) to target dims, or 3) re-run embedding with selected compatible model. We can provide a sample adapter code if you'd like.

customer_acme: Yes please sample adapter would help. Also would appreciate logging hooks so we can detect these regressions earlier — maybe a webhook when a batch has mixed dims.

mahmoud: I'll add a webhook-triggered check to the SDK that warns when mixed dims are detected and logs the model ids used. Ticketing a small SDK patch and a doc snippet about model-to-reranker compatibility.

ashley: Summary for customer: root cause = embedding model swapped to a different-dimension vector (1536) while reranker expects 1024; effect = numerical mismatch causing unexpected scores rather than explicit API errors. Short-term remediation = stop mixed-dim jobs, re-run embeddings with compatible model or normalize/transform vectors, we've opened billing ticket for retries. Long-term: we'll return 400 on dim mismatch and add explicit docs mapping embedding models to compatible rerankers.

customer_acme: Great, thanks team. We'll pause the pipeline and apply the rollback. Please keep me posted when the SDK patch and 400 behavior land so we can re-enable safely. :thumbsup:
